records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: This verse is 21:1 in the Hebrew text, 20:45 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text begins chapter 21 here, with the short oracle against the forest of the south (21:1-5). Many Bibles attach these five verses to chapter 20 as 20:45-49, so their 21:1-32 is 21:6-37 here. Open Word Bible follows the numbering of the Hebrew text it translates, and Ezekiel is cited by the Hebrew numbers. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: "The word of the LORD came to me, saying" keeps the wording set for Jeremiah at each level, here and at verses 6, 13 and 23. The LORD's words that follow take no quotation marks, as in chapter 20.

records.heading: Fire in the forest of the south

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ תֵּימָ֔נָה וְהַטֵּ֖ף אֶל־דָּר֑וֹם וְהִנָּבֵ֛א אֶל־יַ֥עַר הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה נֶֽגֶב׃
records.gloss: Son of man, set your face [the] way toward [the] south, and drip toward [the] south, and prophesy against [the] forest of the field, [the] Negev.
pieces: Son of man, turn to face the south. Preach against the south, and prophesy against the forest land of the Negev.

L.2: Son of man, set your face toward the south, and drip [words] against the south, and prophesy against the forest of the field of the Negev.

R.2: Son of man, turn toward the south. Speak out against the south. Prophesy against the forest of the Negev, the land to the south.

decisions.choice: set your face toward: turn to face, as a sign of the message against it
decisions.reason: The prophet turns toward the place he speaks against; see the note at 6:2. The same command opens the explanation of this oracle in verse 7.

decisions.choice: three words for "south": the south, the southland, the Negev
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses three different words for the south. The last, the Negev, is the dry region in the south of Judah. Seen from Babylon, where Ezekiel lived, the invading army would come down on Judah from the north, so Judah and Jerusalem lie to the "south". Verse 7 explains the picture: the south is Jerusalem, and the forest is the land of Israel.

decisions.choice: drip words: preach, let words fall like drops
decisions.reason: The verb "to drip" is used of preaching, as in Amos 7:16 and Micah 2:6, 11.

decisions.choice: turn to face (B); turn toward (R); preach (B); speak out (R)
alternatives: set your face; drip
decisions.reason: "Set your face toward" follows the wording set for Ezekiel at each level. "Drip" is kept at Literal, with "words" supplied, as in Amos 7:16; Balanced and Readable say "preach" and "speak out". Readable explains that the Negev is the land to the south.

records.source: וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ לְיַ֣עַר הַנֶּ֔גֶב שְׁמַ֖ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֡ה הִנְנִ֣י מַֽצִּית־בְּךָ֣׀אֵ֡שׁ וְאָכְלָ֣ה בְךָ֣ כָל־עֵֽץ־לַח֩ וְכָל־עֵ֨ץ יָבֵ֤שׁ לֹֽא־תִכְבֶּה֙ לַהֶ֣בֶת שַׁלְהֶ֔בֶת וְנִצְרְבוּ־בָ֥הּ כָּל־פָּנִ֖ים מִנֶּ֥גֶב צָפֽוֹנָה׃
records.gloss: And say to [the] forest of the Negev, Hear [the] word of Yahweh; thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Behold, I [am] kindling in you a fire, and it will devour in you every tree green and every tree dry; not will be quenched [the] flame blazing, and will be scorched by it all faces from south to north.
pieces: Say to the forest of the Negev: Hear what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has to say. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to kindle a fire in you, and it will consume every green tree and every dry tree in you. The blazing flame will not be put out, and every face from south to north will be scorched by it.

L.3: And say to the forest of the Negev, Listen to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: See, I am kindling a fire in you, and it will devour in you every green tree and every dry tree; the blazing flame will not be quenched, and all faces from south to north will be scorched by it.

R.3: Tell the forest of the Negev, Listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says. This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to start a fire in you. It will burn up every tree, both green and dry. The blazing flames will not be put out. Everyone from south to north will feel the heat of the fire on their faces.

decisions.choice: every green tree and every dry tree: all, without exception
decisions.reason: Green wood and dry wood together stand for everything in the forest. Verse 8 explains them as "the righteous and the wicked". Jesus uses a similar picture of green and dry wood in Luke 23:31.

decisions.choice: all faces from south to north: everyone in the land
decisions.reason: The fire is so great that every face will feel its heat. "From south to north" means the whole land, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: I am about to kindle (B); I am going to start a fire (R)
alternatives: See, I am kindling
decisions.reason: "See" with a participle marks something God is about to do. Literal keeps "See"; Balanced and Readable put it as an action about to happen, as in Jeremiah 21:4. Readable says what "scorched faces" means.

records.source: וְרָאוּ֙ כָּל־בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בִּֽעַרְתִּ֑יהָ לֹ֖א תִּכְבֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And will see all flesh that I, Yahweh, kindled it; not will it be quenched.
pieces: Everyone will see that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have set it ablaze; it will not be put out.

L.4: And all flesh will see that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, kindled it; it will not be quenched.

R.4: Everyone will see that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, started the fire. No one will be able to put it out.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all people
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for human beings in their weakness, and "all flesh" means everyone (Isaiah 40:5-6). The same words return in verses 9-10.

decisions.choice: everyone
alternatives: all flesh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1); Literal keeps it.

records.source: וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲהָ֖הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֵ֚מָּה אֹמְרִ֣ים לִ֔י הֲלֹ֛א מְמַשֵּׁ֥ל מְשָׁלִ֖ים הֽוּא׃פ
records.gloss: And I said, Ah, Lord Yahweh! They [are] saying of me, Is he not a maker of parables?
pieces: Then I said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! They are saying about me, 'Is he not just telling parables?'"

L.5: Then I said, "Ah, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! They say of me, 'Is he not a speaker of parables?'"

R.5: Then I said, "Oh, Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}! People are saying about me, 'He is only telling riddles!'"

decisions.choice: a speaker of parables: someone who talks in figures and riddles
decisions.reason: The word for parable covers proverbs, riddles and figures of speech (17:2; 24:3). The people dismiss Ezekiel's word as clever pictures with no plain meaning, much as they later enjoy his preaching like a love song and do nothing about it (33:30-32).

decisions.choice: the prophet's complaint, and the LORD's answer in verses 6-12
decisions.reason: The LORD answers by saying the same thing again without the picture: the south is Jerusalem, the forest is the land of Israel, and the fire is the sword (verses 7-9).

decisions.choice: Ezekiel's words in double quotes, the people's words in single quotes
decisions.reason: Ezekiel's own words to God are part of his narrative and take quotation marks, as narrative speech does; the people's saying inside them takes single quotes. "Ah" follows the wording of a plea in Jeremiah ("Ah" / "Ah" / "Oh"). Readable gives the people's question as the scornful statement it is.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.6: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: verse numbers: Hebrew 21:6-37 is 21:1-32 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In many Bibles the five verses before this one are numbered 20:45-49, so this verse and the rest of the chapter (21:6-37 here) are numbered 21:1-32 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ. Ezekiel is cited by the Hebrew numbers.

records.heading: The sword drawn from its sheath

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהַטֵּ֖ף אֶל־מִקְדָּשִׁ֑ים וְהִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, and drip toward [the] sanctuaries, and prophesy against [the] land of Israel.
pieces: Son of man, turn to face Jerusalem. Preach against the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel.

L.7: Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, and drip [words] against the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the land of Israel.

R.7: Son of man, turn toward Jerusalem. Speak out against its holy places. Prophesy against the land of Israel.

decisions.choice: the picture of verse 2 explained
decisions.reason: The three lines match the three lines of verse 2: the south is Jerusalem, the southland is the sanctuaries, and the forest of the Negev is the land of Israel. The fire of verse 3 will be the sword of verse 8.

decisions.choice: the sanctuaries: the temple and its holy places
alternatives: the many holy places of the land
decisions.reason: The word is plural. Beside Jerusalem it most likely means the temple and its courts, the holy places of the city (compare 7:24, where God says he will profane "their holy places").

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֞ לְאַדְמַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֣י אֵלַ֔יִךְ וְהוֹצֵאתִ֥י חַרְבִּ֖י מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ וְהִכְרַתִּ֥י מִמֵּ֖ךְ צַדִּ֥יק וְרָשָֽׁע׃
records.gloss: And say to [the] land of Israel, Thus says Yahweh: Behold, I [am] against you, and I will draw my sword from its sheath, and I will cut off from you righteous and wicked.
pieces: Say to the land of Israel, {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am against you. I will draw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath and cut off both righteous and wicked from among you.

L.8: And say to the land of Israel, Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: See, I [am] against you, and I will draw {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath and cut off from you [both] righteous and wicked.

R.8: Tell the land of Israel, This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am against you. I will pull {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath. I will kill both those who do right and those who do wrong.

decisions.choice: righteous and wicked: the coming disaster will sweep away everyone in the land
alternatives: the wicked only, as the Greek reads ("the unrighteous and the lawless")
decisions.reason: This is the plain meaning of the green and dry trees of verse 3. It sits uneasily beside chapters 9 and 18, where God spares those who mourn over the city's sins (9:4) and judges each person by their own deeds (18:20). The point here is the scale of the disaster: when the sword falls on a city, it does not choose. The Septuagint reads "the unrighteous and the lawless", softening the hard saying; the Hebrew is followed.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD: the divine name alone, not "the Lord GOD"
decisions.reason: Most of Ezekiel's messenger formulas have "the Lord GOD"; this one has the divine name alone, and the translation follows the text.

decisions.choice: those who do right and those who do wrong
alternatives: the righteous and the wicked
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the two kinds of people and says "kill" for "cut off", which here means to put to death by the sword.

records.source: יַ֛עַן אֲשֶׁר־הִכְרַ֥תִּי מִמֵּ֖ךְ צַדִּ֣יק וְרָשָׁ֑ע לָ֠כֵן תֵּצֵ֨א חַרְבִּ֧י מִתַּעְרָ֛הּ אֶל־כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר מִנֶּ֥גֶב צָפֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Because that I will cut off from you righteous and wicked, therefore will go out my sword from its sheath against all flesh from south [to] north.
pieces: Because I will cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword will come out of its sheath against everyone from south to north.

L.9: Because I will cut off from you [both] righteous and wicked, therefore {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword will go out from its sheath against all flesh from south [to] north.

R.9: I will kill both those who do right and those who do wrong. That is why I will pull {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath and use it against everyone from south to north.

decisions.choice: because ... therefore: the verse repeats verse 8 to drive it home
decisions.reason: The first half restates the last words of verse 8, and the second half draws the conclusion: the sword will reach "all flesh", the whole land, as the fire did in verse 3.

decisions.choice: everyone
alternatives: all flesh
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, Balanced and Readable say "everyone" for "all flesh".

records.source: וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הוֹצֵ֥אתִי חַרְבִּ֖י מִתַּעְרָ֑הּ לֹ֥א תָשׁ֖וּב עֽוֹד׃ס
records.gloss: And will know all flesh that I, Yahweh, have drawn out my sword from its sheath; not will it return again.
pieces: Then everyone will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have drawn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword from its sheath; it will not go back again.

L.10: And all flesh will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have drawn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword from its sheath; it will not go back again.

R.10: Then everyone will know that I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have pulled {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sword out of its sheath. I will not put it back.

decisions.choice: all flesh will know that I, the LORD: the book's refrain, widened to all people
decisions.reason: The refrain "you will know that I am the LORD" (see 6:7) here takes the form "all flesh will know that I, the LORD, have ...": everyone will see who has done this.

decisions.choice: it will not return again: the sword will not be sheathed until its work is done
decisions.reason: Compare Isaiah 45:23 and 55:11, where God's word goes out and does not return without doing what he sent it to do.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֥ה בֶן־אָדָ֖ם הֵֽאָנַ֑ח בְּשִׁבְר֤וֹן מָתְנַ֨יִם֙ וּבִמְרִיר֔וּת תֵּֽאָנַ֖ח לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, groan; with breaking of loins and with bitterness groan before their eyes.
pieces: As for you, son of man, groan! Groan before their eyes with a body doubled over and with bitter grief.

L.11: And you, son of man, groan! With breaking loins and with bitterness you shall groan before their eyes.

R.11: Son of man, groan in front of them. Groan as if your body were breaking. Groan with bitter grief.

decisions.choice: breaking loins: anguish that doubles the body over
decisions.reason: The loins, the hips and lower back, are where the body feels strength and pain. A grief that "breaks" them is anguish felt in the whole body, as in Isaiah 21:3 and Nahum 2:11.

decisions.choice: before their eyes: a sign acted out in front of the exiles
decisions.reason: Like Ezekiel's other sign-acts (4:1-5:4; 12:3-7), the groaning is done in public so that people will ask what it means (verse 12).

decisions.choice: with a body doubled over (B); as if your body were breaking (R)
alternatives: with breaking loins
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the body's anguish in plain words (m1).

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־יֹאמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ עַל־מָ֖ה אַתָּ֣ה נֶאֱנָ֑ח וְאָמַרְתָּ֡ אֶל־שְׁמוּעָ֣ה כִֽי־בָאָ֡ה וְנָמֵ֣ס כָּל־לֵב֩ וְרָפ֨וּ כָל־יָדַ֜יִם וְכִהֲתָ֣ה כָל־ר֗וּחַ וְכָל־בִּרְכַּ֨יִם֙ תֵּלַ֣כְנָה מַּ֔יִם הִנֵּ֤ה בָאָה֙ וְנִֽהְיָ֔תָה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And it will be when they say to you, On account of what [are] you groaning? and you shall say, Because of [the] news that [is] coming; and will melt every heart, and will go limp all hands, and will be faint every spirit, and all knees will go [to] water. Behold, it is coming, and it will happen, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: And when they ask you, "Why do you groan?" answer them, "Because of the news, for it is on its way. Every heart will melt, every hand will go limp, every spirit will grow faint, and every knee will be weak as water. It is coming! It will surely happen, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."

L.12: And when they say to you, "Why are you groaning?" you shall say, "Because of the news, for it is coming. Every heart will melt, and all hands will go limp, and every spirit will grow faint, and all knees will run with water. See, it is coming, and it will happen, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."

R.12: When people ask you, "Why are you groaning?" tell them, "Because of the news that is coming. When it comes, everyone will lose courage. Their hands will hang limp. They will feel faint, and their knees will shake. It is coming! It will surely happen, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: melting hearts, limp hands, faint spirits, knees turned to water: utter terror
alternatives: knees wet with urine from fear
decisions.reason: Each picture is a sign of terror: courage melts (Joshua 2:11), hands drop (Jeremiah 6:24), the spirit fails, and the knees give way. The last phrase, also in 7:17, may mean that the knees shake like water, or that people wet themselves for fear.

decisions.choice: the news that is coming: the report of Jerusalem's fall
decisions.reason: The news is not named. It is the disaster of the sword (verses 8-10), and in 24:26 and 33:21 a survivor brings Ezekiel the report that the city has fallen.

decisions.choice: everyone will lose courage ... their knees will shake
alternatives: every heart will melt ... all knees will run with water
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pictures mean (m1). Literal and Balanced keep them. The quotation marks follow the narrative frame: the people's question and Ezekiel's answer are speech within the LORD's instructions to him.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And was [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.13: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the formula as in Jeremiah
decisions.reason: The formula is worded as at verses 1 and 6. A new message begins: the song of the sword (verses 14-22).

records.heading: The song of the sword

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הִנָּבֵא֙ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֑י אֱמֹ֕ר חֶ֥רֶב חֶ֛רֶב הוּחַ֖דָּה וְגַם־מְרוּטָֽה׃
records.gloss: Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says [the] Lord: Say, A sword, a sword, sharpened and also polished!
pieces: Son of man, prophesy and say, The Lord says this: \q Say: A sword, a sword, sharpened and polished!

L.14: Son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord: \q Say: A sword, a sword is sharpened, and also polished!

R.14: Son of man, prophesy. Tell them, This is what the Lord says: \q A sword, a sword is sharpened and polished!

decisions.choice: the song of the sword (verses 14-22): a poem in short, fierce lines
decisions.reason: Verses 14-22 are poetry: short lines, repeated words ("a sword, a sword"; "sharpened", "polished") and cries. Many think it was a war song or a sword dance that Ezekiel took up, with the clapping of hands in verses 19 and 22. Several lines (verses 15, 18, 19, 20) are among the hardest in the book, and the notes say so where they come.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord: "Lord" alone, without the divine name
decisions.reason: Here the formula has only "the Lord" (Adonai), not the usual "the Lord GOD". The text is followed as it stands.

decisions.choice: sharpened and polished: made ready for battle
decisions.reason: A sword was sharpened to cut and polished, or burnished, so that it flashed (verse 15).

decisions.choice: Tell them
alternatives: Say ... Say
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "say" twice. Readable keeps one, since the second only repeats the first. The song (verses 14-22) is set in lines at every level, following the Hebrew accents.

records.source: לְמַ֨עַן טְבֹ֤חַ טֶ֨בַח֙ הוּחַ֔דָּה לְמַעַן־הֱיֵה־לָ֥הּ בָּ֖רָק מֹרָ֑טָּה א֣וֹ נָשִׂ֔ישׂ שֵׁ֥בֶט בְּנִ֖י מֹאֶ֥סֶת כָּל־עֵֽץ׃
records.gloss: In order to slaughter a slaughter it is sharpened; in order that to it [be] lightning, it is polished. Or shall we rejoice? [The] rod of my son despises every tree.
pieces: It is sharpened for slaughter, \q polished to flash like lightning. \q Or should we rejoice? \q The rod of my son despises every tree.

L.15: In order to slaughter a slaughter it is sharpened, \q in order that it may have lightning it is polished. \q Or shall we rejoice? \q The rod of my son despises every tree.

R.15: It is sharpened for killing, \q polished to flash like lightning. \q Should we be glad? \q The rod of my son looks down on every tree.

decisions.choice: Or shall we rejoice? The rod of my son despises every tree: the Hebrew words are kept as they stand; their sense is uncertain
alternatives: the sword despises the royal scepter of Judah ("my son") as if it were mere wood (compare Genesis 49:10)

decisions.choice: that it may have lightning: so that it flashes like lightning

decisions.choice: The rod of my son despises every tree, at every level

decisions.reason: Because the sense is uncertain (m1), every level keeps the Hebrew's words; Readable uses only plainer words.

decisions.reason: The phrase may mean "the sword for the great slaughter" or "the sword of the great one who is slain", perhaps the king. The last verb is found only here; it may mean "surround" or "penetrate", as into the inner rooms of a house.

decisions.choice: the great slaughter
alternatives: the great slain one
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the phrase as "the great slaughter", the most likely sense (m3). Literal keeps the Hebrew's form.

records.heading: The king of Babylon at the fork in the road

records.source: וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן־אָדָ֜ם שִׂים־לְךָ֣׀שְׁנַ֣יִם דְּרָכִ֗ים לָבוֹא֙ חֶ֣רֶב מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ אֶחָ֖ד יֵצְא֣וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וְיָ֣ד בָּרֵ֔א בְּרֹ֥אשׁ דֶּֽרֶךְ־עִ֖יר בָּרֵֽא׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, set for yourself two ways for the coming of [the] sword of [the] king of Babylon; from one land shall go out the two of them; and a hand cut out, at [the] head of [the] way of a city cut [it] out.
pieces: As for you, son of man, mark out two roads that the sword of the king of Babylon may take, both of them starting from one country. Carve a signpost, and set it where the road to a city begins.

L.24: And you, son of man, mark out for yourself two ways for the sword of the king of Babylon to come; from one land the two of them shall go out. And carve a hand; at the head of the way to a city carve [it].

R.24: Son of man, draw two roads that the king of Babylon and his army can take with their swords. Both roads start in the same country. Where the road divides, put up a sign that points the way to a city.

decisions.choice: mark out two roads: a sign-act, perhaps drawn on the ground or on a brick
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, where Ezekiel draws Jerusalem on a brick, he makes a map of the choice the king of Babylon will face.

decisions.choice: a hand: a signpost or marker
decisions.reason: "Hand" is used for a monument or marker (1 Samuel 15:12; 2 Samuel 18:18). Here it is a sign at the fork in the road, perhaps shaped like a hand pointing the way.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon: Nebuchadnezzar, on his campaign against Judah and Ammon
decisions.reason: In 589-588 BC King Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon (2 Kings 24:20), and Ammon seems to have been among the neighbors who plotted with him (Jeremiah 27:3). Nebuchadnezzar marched west to put down the revolt, and Jerusalem was besieged from early 588 BC (2 Kings 25:1).

decisions.choice: a signpost (B); a sign that points the way (R)
alternatives: a hand
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "hand" is (m2). Readable makes plain that the king's sword means his army.

pieces: Mark one road for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another to Judah and to Jerusalem, the fortified city.

L.25: A way you shall mark out by which the sword may come to Rabbah of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon, and [another] to Judah, into Jerusalem the fortified.

R.25: Mark one road that leads the army to Rabbah, the Ammonite capital. Mark the other road to Judah and to Jerusalem, the city with strong walls.

decisions.choice: Rabbah of the Ammonites: the Ammonite capital, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Rabbah lay on the site of modern Amman. Ammon also faced Babylon's anger, and 25:1-7 and 21:33-37 turn to it.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem the fortified: a city that trusted in its walls
decisions.reason: The word stresses the city's strength. It was strong enough to hold out for a year and a half, but not to be saved (2 Kings 25:1-4).

decisions.choice: the children of Ammon (L); the Ammonites (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows Jeremiah 49:2, as published.

pieces: For the king of Babylon has stopped at the fork in the road, where the two roads begin, to look for an omen. He shakes the arrows, consults his household gods and examines the liver.

L.26: For the king of Babylon stands at the mother of the way, at the head of the two ways, to practice divination; he shakes the arrows, he consults the teraphim, he looks at the liver.

R.26: The king of Babylon will stop at the place where the road divides into two. He will look for a sign to show him which way to go. He will shake arrows marked with names. He will ask his household idols for advice. He will look closely at the liver of an animal he has sacrificed.

decisions.choice: the mother of the way: the fork in the road
decisions.reason: The road is pictured as a mother from which the two roads come.

decisions.choice: three ways of seeking an omen: drawing marked arrows, consulting the teraphim, reading the liver
decisions.reason: Arrows with names on them were shaken in a quiver, and the one drawn out gave the answer (verse 27). The teraphim were household gods or images that were consulted (Zechariah 10:2). Reading the liver of a sacrificed animal was a well-known art in Babylon, where clay models of livers marked for omens have been found.

decisions.choice: arrows marked with names; the liver of an animal he has sacrificed
alternatives: the arrows; the liver
decisions.reason: Readable explains each kind of omen (m2). "Teraphim" is "household gods" at Balanced and "household idols" at Readable, as in Hosea 3:4 and Zechariah 10:2.

pieces: The omen for Jerusalem falls into his right hand: to set up battering rams, to give the order to kill, to raise the battle cry, to set battering rams against the gates, to heap up a ramp and to build a siege wall.

L.27: Into his right hand has come the divination: Jerusalem! To set battering rams, to open the mouth with slaughter, to raise the voice with a battle cry, to set battering rams against the gates, to pour out a siege ramp, to build a siege wall.

R.27: The sign in his right hand points to Jerusalem. It tells him to set up battering rams, to shout the order to kill and to raise the war cry. He is to set battering rams against the city gates, pile up dirt ramps against the walls and build siege walls.

decisions.choice: into his right hand comes the omen: the arrow marked "Jerusalem" is drawn
decisions.reason: The king draws the arrow with his right hand, and it bears the name of Jerusalem. The choice of road is made for him, and through it, the text implies, by the LORD.

decisions.choice: to open the mouth with slaughter: to give the order to kill
decisions.reason: To open the mouth is to speak; here the command to slaughter. Some ancient versions read "with a shout".

decisions.choice: battering rams, a siege ramp, a siege wall: the ways of besieging a city
decisions.reason: The same list is used in 4:2 for the siege Ezekiel acts out. Earth was heaped up against the walls so that the rams could reach them, and a wall or line of towers was built around the city to cut it off.

decisions.choice: to give the order to kill
alternatives: to open the mouth with slaughter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m2).

records.source: וְהָיָ֨ה לָהֶ֤ם כִּקְסָם־שָׁוְא֙ בְּעֵ֣ינֵיהֶ֔ם שְׁבֻעֵ֥י שְׁבֻע֖וֹת לָהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא־מַזְכִּ֥יר עָוֺ֖ן לְהִתָּפֵֽשׂ׃פ

pieces: To the people of Jerusalem it will seem a false omen, since they have sworn solemn oaths. But he will bring their guilt to mind, and they will be captured.

L.28: And it will be to them like a false divination in their eyes; they have oaths sworn to them; but he brings [their] guilt to remembrance, so that they will be captured.

R.28: To the people of Jerusalem it will look like a false sign, because they have sworn solemn oaths. But the king of Babylon will remember their guilt, and they will be captured.

decisions.choice: they have sworn solemn oaths: the oaths of loyalty Judah swore to Babylon
alternatives: "they have the most solemn oaths", meaning God's promises, which they trust to protect them
the oaths their own diviners swore that the city would be safe
decisions.reason: The Hebrew, "oaths of oaths to them", is very compressed. The most likely sense is that the people of Jerusalem trusted the solemn oaths they had sworn, either to Babylon or to one another, so that they thought the omen could not be true. Zedekiah had sworn loyalty to Nebuchadnezzar and broken his oath (17:13-19).

decisions.choice: he brings guilt to remembrance: the king of Babylon calls their guilt to account
alternatives: God, who remembers their guilt
decisions.reason: "He" is most likely the king of Babylon, who will remember the broken oath and punish the rebellion. In the end it is also God's judgment (verse 29). "Bring guilt to remembrance" is legal language for calling a wrong to account (Numbers 5:15).

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon
alternatives: he
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who remembers (m2).

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ יַ֗עַן הַזְכַּרְכֶם֙ עֲוֺ֣נְכֶ֔ם בְּהִגָּל֣וֹת פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֗ם לְהֵֽרָאוֹת֙ חַטֹּ֣אותֵיכֶ֔ם בְּכֹ֖ל עֲלִילֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם יַ֚עַן הִזָּ֣כֶרְכֶ֔ם בַּכַּ֖ף תִּתָּפֵֽשׂוּ׃פ
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because you have caused to be remembered your guilt, in [that] your transgressions are uncovered, so that your sins appear in all your deeds; because you have been remembered, by the hand you will be seized.
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: You have brought your guilt to mind by your open rebellion, so that your sins show in everything you do. Because you have been called to account, you will be taken captive.

L.29: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because you have brought your guilt to remembrance, in that your transgressions are uncovered, so that your sins appear in all your deeds; because you have come to remembrance, you will be seized by the hand.

R.29: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: You have made everyone remember your guilt. Your rebellion is out in the open, and your sins show in everything you do. Because of this, you will be called to account and taken prisoner.

decisions.choice: remembered: called to account, a play on verse 28
decisions.reason: The verb "remember" runs through verses 28-29 and 37. The people's guilt is "remembered", brought before the judge; they themselves have "been remembered", called to account. In verse 37 Ammon "will not be remembered" at all.

decisions.choice: seized by the hand: taken captive
decisions.reason: To be taken "by the hand" is to fall into an enemy's power.

decisions.choice: transgressions (L); rebellion (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word for transgression follows the wording settled for the prophets: "transgression" (L), "rebellion" (B), "sin" (R). Readable uses "rebellion" here so that it is not the same word as the "sins" that follow.

records.source: וְאַתָּה֙ חָלָ֣ל רָשָׁ֔ע נְשִׂ֖יא יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣א יוֹמ֔וֹ בְּעֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן קֵֽץ׃ס
records.gloss: And you, profane, wicked, prince of Israel, whose day has come, in [the] time of [the] iniquity of [the] end,
pieces: As for you, profane and wicked prince of Israel, your day has come, the time of final punishment.

L.30: And you, profane [and] wicked one, prince of Israel, whose day has arrived, in the time of the punishment of the end,

R.30: And you, wicked ruler of Israel, who has treated holy things with contempt, your day has come. It is the time of your final punishment.

decisions.choice: the prince of Israel: King Zedekiah
decisions.reason: Ezekiel calls Zedekiah "the prince" (12:10, 12) and does not use the word "king" for him. Zedekiah had broken his oath to Babylon (17:15-19) and, after the city fell, was blinded and taken to Babylon (2 Kings 25:6-7).

decisions.choice: profane: one who has treated holy things as common
alternatives: "pierced" or "slain", as the same word means in verses 19 and 34
decisions.reason: The word can mean "profane" or "pierced, slain". Zedekiah was not killed in battle, so "profane" fits him better here; but the play with the slain of the sword in the song is clear.

decisions.choice: the time of the iniquity of the end: the time when guilt brings final punishment
decisions.reason: The word for iniquity can mean guilt and also the punishment it brings. The same phrase is used in 21:34 and 35:5.

decisions.choice: who has treated holy things with contempt; ruler
alternatives: profane; prince
decisions.reason: Readable says what "profane" means (m2), and uses "ruler" for "prince", as set for Ezekiel. The comma at Literal shows that the address runs on into the commands of verse 31.

records.heading: A word to the prince of Israel

records.source: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הָסִיר֙ הַמִּצְנֶ֔פֶת וְהָרִ֖ים הָֽעֲטָרָ֑ה זֹ֣את לֹא־זֹ֔את הַשָּׁפָ֣לָה הַגְבֵּ֔הַוְהַגָּבֹ֖הַהַשְׁפִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Remove the turban, and take off the crown! This [is] not this. The low exalt, and the high bring low.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Take away the turban and lift off the crown! Things will not stay as they are. Raise up the low and bring down the high.

L.31: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Take off the turban, and remove the crown! This [will] not [be] this. Exalt the low, and bring low the high.

R.31: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Take off the king's turban, and remove his crown. Nothing will stay as it is. Lift up those who are low, and bring down those who are high.

decisions.choice: the turban and the crown: signs of rule
alternatives: the high priest's turban, so that priesthood and kingship both end
decisions.reason: The word for turban is used elsewhere for the high priest's headdress (Exodus 28:4, 37), but here it stands beside the crown as a sign of the ruler's office. Some take it to mean that both the priestly and the royal offices come to an end with Jerusalem's fall.

decisions.choice: this is not this: things will not remain as they are
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is a short saying, literally "this not this". It means that the present order is about to be overturned, as the next words say.

decisions.choice: exalt the low, bring low the high: God overturns the powerful
decisions.reason: The same reversal is sung by Hannah (1 Samuel 2:7-8) and by Mary (Luke 1:52), and Ezekiel uses it of the trees in 17:24.

decisions.choice: the king's turban; his crown
alternatives: the turban; the crown
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain whose turban and crown are meant (verse 30).

records.source: עַוָּ֥ה עַוָּ֖ה עַוָּ֣ה אֲשִׂימֶ֑נָּה גַּם־זֹאת֙ לֹ֣א הָיָ֔ה עַד־בֹּ֛א אֲשֶׁר־ל֥וֹ הַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט וּנְתַתִּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it; also this not will be, until comes [he] whom to him [is] the judgment, and I will give it.
pieces: A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! Even this will be no more, until he comes to whom the right belongs, and I will give it to him.

L.32: A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! This also will not be, until he comes to whom the judgment [belongs], and I will give it [to him].

R.32: I will make it a ruin, a ruin, a ruin! It will be gone until the one comes who has the right to it. I will give it to him.

decisions.choice: until he comes to whom it belongs: an echo of Genesis 49:10
alternatives: the one to whom judgment is given, meaning Nebuchadnezzar, who will carry out God's judgment on Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The words recall Jacob's blessing of Judah: "the scepter shall not depart from Judah ... until he comes to whom it belongs" (Genesis 49:10, as many read it). Here the kingship is overturned and left in ruins until the rightful one comes; Ezekiel speaks later of a coming shepherd-king from David's line (34:23-24; 37:24). The word translated "right" also means "judgment", and some take the verse to mean the one appointed to carry out judgment. Later Jewish and Christian readers took the verse as a promise of the Messiah. The text does not name him.

decisions.choice: a ruin, a ruin, a ruin: the threefold word for complete overthrow
decisions.reason: Repeating a word three times makes it as strong as Hebrew can, as in "holy, holy, holy" (Isaiah 6:3). What will be ruined is the kingship of verse 31.

decisions.choice: the right (B); the right to it (R)
alternatives: the judgment
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the word chosen in m1; Literal keeps "the judgment". The one who comes is not named, so no pronoun for him takes the capitalized setting.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם הִנָּבֵ֤א וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וְאֶל־חֶרְפָּתָ֑ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ חֶ֣רֶב חֶ֤רֶב פְּתוּחָה֙ לְטֶ֣בַח מְרוּטָ֔ה לְהָכִ֖יל לְמַ֥עַן בָּרָֽק׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh concerning [the] sons of Ammon and concerning their reproach; and say, A sword, a sword drawn, for slaughter polished, to consume, in order to [be] lightning,
pieces: And you, son of man, prophesy and say, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this about the Ammonites and their taunts. Say: A sword, a sword is drawn for slaughter, polished to devour and to flash like lightning,

L.33: And you, son of man, prophesy and say, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} concerning the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ammon and concerning their taunting; and say: A sword, a sword is drawn, polished for slaughter, to consume, so as to be like lightning,

R.33: Son of man, prophesy. Say, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says about the Ammonites, who mock Israel: A sword, a sword is drawn to kill! It is polished to destroy and to flash like lightning.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites and their taunting: Ammon mocked Judah's fall
decisions.reason: Ammon rejoiced over the ruin of the temple and the land (25:3, 6). Zephaniah 2:8 also speaks of the "taunts" of the Ammonites. Though the king of Babylon chose Jerusalem first (verse 27), Ammon will not escape.

decisions.choice: a sword, a sword: the song of verses 14-15 taken up again
decisions.reason: The words of the sword song return, now turned against Ammon.

decisions.choice: who mock Israel
alternatives: their taunting
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the Ammonites taunted. The comma at Literal and Balanced shows that the sentence runs on into verse 34.

records.heading: A sword against the Ammonites

records.source: בַּחֲז֥וֹת לָךְ֙ שָׁ֔וְא בִּקְסָם־לָ֖ךְ כָּזָ֑ב לָתֵ֣ת אוֹתָ֗ךְ אֶֽל־צַוְּארֵי֙ חַֽלְלֵ֣י רְשָׁעִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֣א יוֹמָ֔ם בְּעֵ֖ת עֲוֺ֥ן קֵֽץ׃
records.gloss: while they see for you worthless [visions], while they divine for you a lie, to put you on [the] necks of [the] slain wicked ones, whose day has come, in [the] time of [the] iniquity of [the] end.
pieces: while they see false visions for you and divine lies for you, to lay you on the necks of the slain, the wicked, whose day has arrived, the time of their final punishment.

L.34: while they see empty visions for you, while they divine lies for you, to lay you on the necks of the slain, the wicked, whose day has arrived, in the time of the punishment of the end.

R.34: False prophets see visions for you that mean nothing and tell lies about the future. But the sword will be laid on the necks of the wicked who are to be killed. Their day has come, the time of their final punishment.

decisions.choice: "you" here is the sword, laid on the necks of the wicked; false prophets promise safety
alternatives: "you" is Ammon, whose diviners deceive it, and which will be laid among the slain
decisions.reason: The "you" is feminine in Hebrew, like the word "sword". The sword is laid on the necks of the wicked while the diviners offer false comfort. The same "you" in verses 35-37 is then most likely Ammon (see verse 35). The verses are hard, and who is addressed is not certain.

decisions.choice: the slain: the same word as "profane" in verse 30
decisions.reason: Here the plural clearly means people killed by the sword, and with "the wicked" it echoes the description of Zedekiah in verse 30.

decisions.choice: false prophets ...; the sword will be laid on the necks
alternatives: they see ... for you; to lay you on the necks
decisions.reason: Readable names those who see false visions, and says "the sword" for the feminine "you", following m1.

records.source: הָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־תַּעְרָ֑הּ בִּמְק֧וֹם אֲשֶׁר־נִבְרֵ֛את בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מְכֻרוֹתַ֖יִךְ אֶשְׁפֹּ֥ט אֹתָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Return [it] to its sheath! In [the] place where you were created, in [the] land of your origin, I will judge you.
pieces: Put the sword back in its sheath! Where you were created, in the land of your birth, there I will judge you.

L.35: Return [it] to its sheath! In the place in which you were created, in the land of your origins, I will judge you.

R.35: Put the sword back into its sheath! I will judge you in the place where you were made, in the land where you began.

decisions.choice: the one addressed is Ammon: it will be judged in its own land
alternatives: Babylon, God's sword, which will itself be judged in its own land once its work is done (as Jeremiah 50-51)
decisions.reason: After the sword has done its work, the one addressed is told to put it away and is judged "in the land of your origin". Ammon fits this, since verse 37 says "you will not be remembered", as 25:10 says of Ammon. Some take the verses as a word against Babylon, the sword of God, which will in turn be judged.

decisions.choice: the sword
alternatives: it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no object for "return"; the sheath shows that the sword is meant.

records.source: וְשָׁפַכְתִּ֤י עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ זַעְמִ֔י בְּאֵ֥שׁ עֶבְרָתִ֖י אָפִ֣יחַ עָלָ֑יִךְ וּנְתַתִּ֗יךְ בְּיַד֙ אֲנָשִׁ֣ים בֹּֽעֲרִ֔ים חָרָשֵׁ֖י מַשְׁחִֽית׃
records.gloss: And I will pour out on you my indignation; with [the] fire of my wrath I will blow on you, and I will give you into [the] hand of men brutal, craftsmen of destruction.
pieces: I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation on you and blow on you with the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath. I will hand you over to brutal men, skilled at destroying.

L.36: And I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} indignation on you; with the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath I will blow on you, and I will give you into the hand of brutal men, craftsmen of destruction.

R.36: I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on you. I will breathe out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fiery anger against you. I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts at destroying.

decisions.choice: blow on you with the fire of my wrath: like a smith blowing on a forge
decisions.reason: The picture is of air blown on a fire to make it hotter. Ezekiel uses it at length for Jerusalem in 22:20-21.

decisions.choice: brutal men, craftsmen of destruction
decisions.reason: The first word is used of senseless, brutish people (Psalm 92:7). The second, "craftsmen" or "smiths", fits the forge of the first half: the one who was "created" (verse 35) is handed over to men skilled only in destroying.

records.source: לָאֵ֤שׁ תִּֽהְיֶה֙ לְאָכְלָ֔ה דָּמֵ֥ךְ יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאָ֑רֶץ לֹ֣א תִזָּכֵ֔רִי כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי׃פ
records.gloss: For the fire you will be fuel; your blood will be in [the] midst of the land; not will you be remembered, for I, Yahweh, have spoken.
pieces: You will be fuel for the fire, and your blood will be spilled in the land. You will be remembered no more, for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.

L.37: You will be fuel for the fire; your blood will be in the midst of the land; you will be remembered no more, for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.

R.37: You will be burned up like wood in a fire. Your blood will be spilled in your land. No one will remember you, because I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, have spoken.

decisions.choice: you will not be remembered: a people that will vanish from memory
decisions.reason: The same words are said of Ammon in 25:10. To be forgotten was the end of a people's name and life.

decisions.choice: I, the LORD, have spoken: the closing seal
decisions.reason: The chapter ends as the sword song did (verse 22).

decisions.choice: spilled
alternatives: your blood will be in the midst of the land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what blood "in the land" means.
